competitors.rationale: Verified on 2026-07-30 (C:MealLoop). Strongly established among families with automated weekly dinner planning, grocery lists, and family sharing, though it lacks pantry/fridge inventory tracking.

Last verified on 2024-11-05 (C:PlanPlate), making details possibly outdated. It offers basic calendar meal planning and shared plans for couples/flatmates, but lacks inventory tracking and automated lists.
Verified on 2026-06-18 (C:PantryGenie). Strong on pantry inventory tracking via barcode scanning and expiry alerts with a shopping list, but does not provide end-to-end weekly dinner planning.

competitors.rationale: Verified on 2026-05-02 but lacks a source URL, so its row details must be marked unsourced (C:WeekWise). Focuses on budget weekly meal planning and store price comparisons, but lacks inventory awareness.

Last verified on 2025-01-20 via a homepage rather than a pricing page (C:ZeroWaste Kitchen), making it possibly outdated. Focuses on ad-hoc leftover recipes rather than structured weekly planning or inventory management.

Verified on 2026-08-25 (C:SupperSync). Targets shared households with weekly plans, chore assignment, and shopping lists, directly competing on household coordination, but does not know on-hand inventory.

white_space: No single competitor integrates existing fridge/pantry inventory tracking with automated weekly dinner planning and shared household shopping lists. Current offerings either track inventory without planning (C:FridgeChef, C:PantryGenie) or plan meals without knowing on-hand items (C:MealLoop, C:PlanPlate, C:SupperSync, C:WeekWise).

No competitor combines household coordination and chore assignment (covered by C:SupperSync) with food waste reduction and inventory expiry tracking (covered by C:PantryGenie and C:ZeroWaste Kitchen).
pricing_anchors: Competitor monthly list prices range from EUR 2.99/month (C:PlanPlate; stale) to EUR 6.99/month (C:MealLoop, with an annual option of EUR 49.99/year, converting to ~EUR 4.17/month). Other active competitors charge EUR 3.99/month (C:PantryGenie), EUR 4.49/month per household (C:SupperSync), and EUR 4.99/month (C:FridgeChef). Market survey data indicates a median stated willingness to pay for a cooking app of EUR 3.50 per month (S05). Any pricing hypothesis above EUR 6.99/month is entirely untested by existing market benchmarks.

idea_claim_checks.claim: Existing recipe apps give ideas but do not know what you already own.
idea_claim_checks.explanation: Contradicted by competitor records. C:FridgeChef identifies on-hand ingredients from fridge photos to suggest recipes, and C:PantryGenie tracks pantry inventory via barcode scanning with expiry alerts. The genuine market differentiation lies in pairing inventory awareness with multi-day weekly planning, not inventory tracking alone.

idea_claim_checks.claim: Dinner planning is a daily chore, groceries are expensive, and a lot of food gets thrown away.
idea_claim_checks.explanation: Supported by market statistics: S04 reports adults spend 22 minutes daily deciding what to cook (with the caveat that S04 is from 2023), S02 demonstrates significant expenditure at EUR 118 per week for two-person households, and S01 establishes food waste at 19% of purchased food.
